Package main.java.progOO2.p08

package main.java.progOO2.p08

Programming Object Oriented II: DecreasingCounter

This package introduces the concept of modifying an object's internal state through method calls. The DecreasingCounter class serves as a basic example of a mutable object — one whose attributes can change after instantiation.

Key learning goals:

  • State change through methods: The decrement() method demonstrates how the value of an instance variable can be changed based on a condition.
  • Control structures: Students apply conditional logic to prevent the counter from going below zero.
  • Reset behavior: The reset() method shows how an object's state can be restored to a default value.
  • Encapsulation: The value field is private, so any changes to it must be done through class methods, reinforcing encapsulation.

This exercise helps students understand how objects can have behavior that modifies internal data, and prepares them for the concepts of validation, state management, and method interaction.

Note: The DecreasingCounter class is intended to support hands-on practice with mutability and basic defensive programming (e.g., preventing negative values).
